headline: GOLD AND SILVER EACH RALLY 1% DAY AFTER FED HIKE — WARSH WITHHOLDS DOT AS $4,300 FLOOR HOLDS
snippet: Spot gold and silver each surged approximately 1% on September 17, 2026, recovering to near $4,300 and $64/oz respectively after the Fed's unanimous 25bp hike — with Chairman Warsh's decision to withhold his dot (leaving only 18 of 19 FOMC forecasts) injecting fresh uncertainty about whether the signalled additional hike will actually materialize, as markets interpreted the unusual step as ambiguity rather than additional hawkishness.

headline: ORDELL DRILLS 19M AT 2.70 G/T AU FROM 40M DEPTH — McNABS EAST 122-HOLE RC PROGRAM UNDERWAY, MRE TARGETED Q4 2026
snippet: Ordell Minerals (ASX: ORD) released the first 11 holes from its 122-hole RC drill program at McNabs East within the Barimaia Gold Project in Western Australia on September 17, with intercepts starting approximately 10 metres below surface including 32m at 1.65 g/t Au, 19m at 2.70 g/t Au from 40m, and 25m at 1.89 g/t Au from 16m — results from the remaining 111 holes are expected over six weeks, with a maiden Mineral Resource Estimate targeted for the December 2026 quarter.

headline: AURO DRILLS 905M AT 0.60 G/T AU IN ECUADOR — DEEPEST HOLE YET CONFIRMS OPEN AT DEPTH, PHASE II 20,000M BEGINS
snippet: Auro Metals (TSXV: AURO) intersected 905.22 metres at 0.60 g/t gold and 0.12% copper from 56.5m in hole DSB-68 at its Santa Barbara Gold-Copper Project in Ecuador — the longest and deepest hole drilled to date, reaching 1,282 metres and remaining mineralized to the end of hole — alongside DSB-70 returning 262.5m at 0.71 g/t Au; with Phase I at 11,047m complete, the company has launched a 20,000m Phase II targeting depth and strike extensions of what appears to be a large bulk-mineable porphyry system.

headline: METALSOURCE DRILLS 261 G/T AGEQ OVER 7M AT 245M DEPTH — SILVER HILL ENTERS MAJOR EXPANSION PHASE
snippet: Metalsource Mining (CSE: MSM) reported September 16 that hole SH26-22 returned 7.32 metres at 261 g/t silver equivalent — including 1.37 metres at 930 g/t AgEq from 245.67m — and hole SH26-23 returned 12.31 metres at 140 g/t AgEq at depth at Silver Hill in Nevada; management cited the consistent deep continuity as the trigger for a major expansion phase with additional drill rigs targeting the down-dip extension of what the company calls North America's most active new primary silver development.

headline: COPPER MARKET STUCK BETWEEN LME RECORD AND TARIFF REVERSAL — PHYSICAL SQUEEZE CONTINUES AS INVENTORIES SPLIT
snippet: Copper settled into a standoff between the September 8 LME all-time high of $14,533/tonne and a nearly 5% pullback on reports the U.S. is reconsidering refined metal tariffs — with the split leaving COMEX inventories at record highs while LME on-warrant stocks sit near five-month lows and LME backwardation signals physical buyers are paying significant premiums for prompt delivery outside the U.S., a structural divergence that analysts say can only be resolved by either tariff clarity or a demand correction.

headline: RARE EARTHS: CHINA EXPORT CONTROL SUSPENSION EXPIRES NOV 10 — $6.5 TRILLION IN GLOBAL ECONOMIC EXPOSURE IS ON THE CLOCK
snippet: A September 2026 analysis from Mining Stock Education frames China's November 10 and November 27 expiry dates — when the November 2025 diplomatic suspension of rare earth, gallium, germanium and antimony export restrictions lapses and the underlying licensing regime returns — as the clearest single market catalyst on the calendar, noting that the IEA estimates $6.5 trillion in annual global economic activity is exposed to a full reimplementation, with dysprosium, terbium, and yttrium supply chains the most structurally vulnerable.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: MINERS DELIVERED 54% vs. FLAT BULLION — HERE IS THE ACTUAL LEVERAGE MATH AND ITS LIMITS
snippet: GoldSilver.com's September 2026 analysis quantifies the two-to-three-times operating leverage of gold mining businesses — explaining why a 1% gold price increase can generate 2-3% margin expansion — while also cataloguing the structural risks miners carry that physical gold never does: reserve depletion, execution risk, balance sheet exposure, and geopolitical jurisdiction; the piece argues that post-FOMC, cost structure is now the primary differentiator and low-AISC producers are the only miner class worth owning at current P/NAV levels.

headline: SPROTT MONEY: GOLD UP 10.5% AND SILVER 14.9% IN AUGUST — SEPTEMBER FED HIKE IS THE BULL MARKET'S FIRST REAL TEST
snippet: Sprott Money's September 2026 update reviews the extraordinary August performance — gold up 10.5% and silver 14.9% in a single month on central bank buying and Middle East supply disruptions — and argues the September Fed decision is the first real bull market stress test, identifying $4,900/oz as the breakout price that would force institutional managers carrying zero precious metals exposure into the market and drive the next leg of the cycle.

headline: GOLD MINERS TURNING HIGHER ON SCHEDULE — SEASONAL AND TECHNICAL SIGNALS ALIGN POST-FOMC
snippet: Market Zeitgeist's September 2026 technical analysis identifies converging signals for a gold and silver miner recovery: the sector's historical Q3 seasonal low aligns with the post-FOMC reset in rate expectations, GDX is holding key support at 13-year highs relative to bullion, and junior miners tracked by GDXJ are coiling near $126–$127 with above-average volume suggesting institutional accumulation ahead of year-end resource market seasonality.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD'S NEXT SURGE — WHY STRUCTURAL DEMAND MAKES 2026 DIFFERENT FROM PRIOR RATE-HIKE CYCLES
snippet: GoldSeek's September 2026 analysis argues the current gold market is structurally different from the 2018 and 2022 rate-hike cycles: central bank buying is running at 289 tonnes per quarter, the BRICS gold-trade settlement framework is absorbing physical supply, and de-dollarisation flows are providing a demand floor independent of real yields — making the traditional inverse gold-rates relationship increasingly unreliable as a trading framework for the current environment.
